fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled fuzz input bytes are stored as the fuzz data state, including TLV response payloads that will be sent back to the IMAP client.
The first response TLV bytes are stored as the server response data that will be written to the socket when the IMAP client connects.
The attacker-controlled response bytes are selected for writing to the IMAP server socket.
The attacker-controlled response bytes are written to the socket, becoming the IMAP server response that curl will parse.
The server response is read into data->state.buffer, which is allocated as buffer_size+1 bytes. The read loop stops when nread_resp reaches buffer_size.

fine_trace.code: size_t n = ptr - pp->linestart_resp; memmove(buf, pp->linestart_resp, n); buf[n] = 0;
fine_trace.note: The final response line is copied to the start of the buffer and zero-terminated at position n, where n can be up to buffer_size.
The IMAP LIST/SEARCH response line is taken from data->state.buffer. strlen(line) can return up to buffer_size when the line fills the entire buffer.

A newline is written at buffer[len]. When len equals buffer_size, this writes at buffer[buffer_size], which is the last valid byte of the buffer_size+1 allocation. However, when the line is exactly buffer_size bytes and the zero terminator is at position buffer_size, strlen returns buffer_size and the write is at the boundary.
The line including the appended newline is passed to the write callback, which copies it into the fuzzer's write_array buffer.

The write callback copies the body data into the fixed-size write_array[10] stack buffer. When the IMAP response line is large, this copy overflows the 10-byte stack buffer, causing a stack-buffer-overflow WRITE.
